absent: Full field layout of early allocator container, region descriptor and per CPU construction descriptor beyond members observed here.
Locking and concurrency rules for reservation insertion, merge, flag mutation and distance teardown.
Exact platform hook contracts for CPU to node translation and NUMA discovery plus distance values.
Virtual area registration, page table population details and mapping error paths beyond abort behaviour.
Leak detector scanning, reference counting and teardown beyond creation linkage.
Allocator direction policy, current limit management and post slab handover behaviour.

findings.text: Early physical reservation offers a virtual address variant bounded by the current allocator ceiling with retry without lower limit on first miss, signalling exhaustion with null and otherwise returning a kernel mapping; the trying variant additionally clears granted bytes.

Range reservation from the early pool diverts to node aware slab allocation with a one time warning once slab service is available, supplies a cache default when alignment is unspecified with a diagnostic, favours the requested node before any node unless exact placement was demanded, and downgrades mirrored requests with throttled notice, signalling total failure with zero.

Reservation marking delegates to a generic ordered range inserter treating an empty container as direct install, otherwise measuring needed disjoint gaps, growing the container until sufficient, installing gaps, and coalescing neighbours with matching ownership and attributes.

The ordered extent table preserves address order, forbids overlap, coalesces only neighbours that abut exactly while sharing node association and flags, and keeps count plus total size consistent across insertion, growth and merge.

The per CPU construction descriptor records group multiplicity and page aligned total footprint, aligns its header so the following CPU map is suitably placed, obtains backing from early page granular reservation, and initializes every map entry to an out of range sentinel denoting unassigned.
A constructed per CPU layout must account exactly for the expected unit population; any mismatch is treated as a fatal boot inconsistency.

First chunk creation is an early boot entry requiring a single group layout and page granularity; on success it guarantees one mapped unit per possible processor with replicated static image and announced sizing, on page shortage it guarantees release of partial pages with resource exhaustion signalling, and on mapping failure it aborts boot.

NUMA bring up is an early boot entry that on success guarantees cleared prior state, platform discovered extents cleaned and registered, coverage validated, per node descriptors materialized and parsed nodes online; on discovery or validation failure it guarantees distance teardown and error return.
Translation from page frame to node identity serializes access to a small last range cache with a dedicated early spinlock held across cache probe, table search and fallback selection.

Leak tracker registration allocates its tracking record outside any lock, then holds an interrupt masking raw spinlock only while linking the record into global state, releasing the record after unlock when linkage reports failure; physical registration applies a physical marker and zero minimum reference.

Invoking the early range allocator after slab availability is diagnosed as misuse with fallback semantics, zero alignment is diagnosed with substitution of a cache default, and address search outside all extents yields a not found sentinel that propagates as unknown node.
Mirrored early allocation behaves as a two state policy that first requires mirrored backing and upon failure downgrades to unmirrored backing with a rate limited notice before declaring failure.

Per node control storage guarantees publication through an indexed table with cleared content stamped with identity and aggregated span; it prefers node local early backing with fallback to any early backing, aborts boot when none exists, and still materializes descriptors for memory less nodes with an announcement.
Aggregation of frame bounds for a node guarantees the tightest span covering all contributing intervals, and guarantees a zero start when no interval contributes.

Frame to node lookup guarantees ownership of the containing extent with frame converted bounds or an unknown marker when outside all extents, using ordered search with a last hit cache to avoid repeated work.

Per CPU page supply prefers node local early backing selected through a platform hook, and when no hook exists or the indicated node is offline or lacks control storage it falls back to generic constrained early reservation with an informational notice.

Coverage checking tallies frames attributed to invalid nodes, fails boot registration when lost bytes exceed a caller threshold while reporting lost versus total megabytes, with total size sourced from the memory table aggregate.
Attribute and ownership changes guarantee that only the affected span is retagged for flags or node association, with neighbours rejoined where attributes again match.

Every successful early range grant passes through post handling that conditionally notifies the leak detector about physical ownership and submits the extent to a platform acceptance hook required by confidential guests before the address is handed out.

Early per CPU mapping guarantees valid intermediate translation tables with missing tables sourced from aborting early reservation, and guarantees installed kernel mappings that preserve caller reclaim constraints through an applied allocation scope.
A physical address early allocator exposes node preference without exactness over the accessible window starting at zero.
First chunk assembly treats page exhaustion as recoverable with unwind and error return, while virtual mapping failure is fatal.
Distance table teardown guarantees no retained storage with count cleared and pointer nulled to rearm creation, releasing prior storage only when a count indicates presence.
Release of first chunk scratch pages returns them to the early pool.
